columns.name: Label.
columns.size_m: Size of the charged object, m.
columns.charge_low_c: Lowest known net charge magnitude of the class.
columns.charge_high_c: Highest known net charge magnitude of the class.
columns.charge_example_c: Net charge magnitude of the marked example object.
columns.charge_max_c: Maximum allowable net charge magnitude; empty if none.
columns.source_url: Primary source for the values (journal DOI, agency fact sheet, spec sheet).
columns.citation: Short citation: authors, year, title, venue.
columns.notes: One line shown in the hover tooltip.

rows.name: Electron
rows.citation: Tiesinga E. et al., CODATA 2022 recommended values, NIST
rows.notes: One elementary charge; size is its Compton wavelength

rows.name: Proton
rows.citation: Tiesinga E. et al., CODATA 2022 recommended values, NIST
rows.notes: Surface field far above the Schwinger value: fine below the Compton scale

rows.name: Uranium nucleus
rows.citation: Angeli I. & Marinova K.P. (2013) Table of experimental nuclear ground state charge radii: an update. ADNDT 99, 69

rows.name: Millikan oil drop
rows.citation: Millikan R.A. (1913) On the elementary electrical charge and the Avogadro constant. Phys Rev 2, 109
rows.notes: Charges were always whole multiples of e

rows.name: Lightning stroke (charge lowered)
rows.citation: Rakov V.A. & Uman M.A. (2003) Lightning: Physics and Effects. Cambridge University Press
rows.notes: About 5 C per return stroke; positive flashes up to hundreds of coulombs

rows.name: Earth's surface charge
rows.citation: Feynman R.P., Leighton R.B. & Sands M. The Feynman Lectures on Physics, Vol. II, ch. 9: Electricity in the atmosphere
rows.notes: Computed from the 100 V/m fair-weather field

rows.name: Sun's net charge
rows.citation: Neslusan L. (2001) On the global electrostatic charge of stars. A&A 372, 913
rows.notes: About 77 C: electrons escape until the star is slightly positive

rows.name: Interplanetary dust grain
rows.citation: Horanyi M. (1996) Charged dust dynamics in the solar system. ARA&A 34, 383
rows.notes: Sunlight knocks out photoelectrons until the grain sits near +5 V: about 1700 e on a 1 micron grain (computed)

rows.name: Levitated droplet at the Rayleigh limit
rows.citation: Duft D. et al. (2003) Rayleigh jets from levitated microdroplets. Nature 421, 128
rows.notes: Ethylene glycol drop bursts into jets at 24 micron radius; charge computed from the Rayleigh limit (surface tension 0.048 N/m)

rows.name: Thunderstorm raindrop
rows.citation: Takahashi T. (1973) Measurement of electric charge of cloud droplets, drizzle, and raindrops. Rev Geophys 11, 903
rows.notes: Largest charges observed in storms follow about 42 r^2 elementary charges (r in microns): 7 pC on a 2 mm drop

rows.name: Person after walking on carpet
rows.citation: IEC 61000-4-2:2008 Electromagnetic compatibility: electrostatic discharge immunity test (150 pF body charged to up to 15 kV)
rows.notes: 150 pF charged to 15 kV: the shock you feel from a door handle

rows.name: ATS-6 satellite in eclipse
rows.citation: Olsen R.C. & Purvis C.K. (1983) Observations of charging dynamics. J Geophys Res 88, 5657
rows.notes: Charged to -19 kV by hot magnetospheric electrons; charge computed for a 3 m body

rows.name: LHC proton beam (one ring)
rows.citation: Bruning O.S. et al. (eds.) (2004) LHC Design Report Vol. 1: The LHC Main Ring. CERN-2004-003
rows.notes: 2808 bunches of 1.15e11 protons circling a 27 km ring

rows.name: Thundercloud main negative charge
rows.citation: Rakov V.A. & Uman M.A. (2003) Lightning: Physics and Effects. Cambridge University Press
rows.notes: Classic tripole: about -40 C a few kilometres across at 6-8 km altitude (size approximate)

rows.name: Sagittarius A* (Milky Way black hole)
rows.citation: Zajacek M. et al. (2018) On the charge of the Galactic centre black hole. MNRAS 480, 4408
rows.notes: Observational upper limit; the size is the horizon diameter of 4.3 million solar masses
